- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots; apply downward correction of 2–5% in subsequent days.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model frequently underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias: if price deviates >3σ from 30-day moving average, correct forecast toward average with decay factor of 0.8 per day.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to over-predict early in the forecast window (first 5–7 days); apply linear decay correction starting from day 5.
- When sentiment flips from bullish to bearish (or vice versa), model lags by 1–3 days; adjust forecast to align with sentiment shift 1–2 days ahead.
